raw_response:
I am going to farm my 7 mu of cotton this year like I have for many years. I do not know how to read much, but I have been doing this since I was thirty, so my hands know the work.

I will buy the same cotton seed my neighbors buy — the kind with the worm protection built in. Everyone around here uses it. Before, when we used old seed, the bollworms ate everything and we had to spray and spray. Now it is better, but we still spray for the other bugs — aphids, the small green ones, the mirids that suck the buds. I spray maybe 7 or 8 times through the season. If I see bugs, I spray. If the neighbor sprays, I spray too.

For fertilizer, I do what I did last year. I buy 2 bags of compound fertilizer (each bag 50 jin — that is about 25 kg) per mu before planting, and then I put urea when the plants start making bolls, about half a bag per mu. So on 7 mu that is 14 bags of compound and about 4 bags of urea. My man carries them from the shop on the three-wheeler. Fertilizer is expensive, but if I use too little, the bolls are small and fall off. Better to put a little extra than lose the harvest. That would be a disaster.

I plough the field with the small tractor the village man brings — he charges by the mu. Then I lay the plastic film and plant underneath. The film keeps the ground warm and keeps water in.

I water from the well. Cotton does not like too much water, but in summer when it is hot and the plants are flowering, I water 3 times. If the rain comes good, maybe only 2 times.

Last year I got about 250 kg of seed cotton per mu. I hope for the same. Some years are better, some worse — it depends on the weather and the bugs.
